claims.text: Chemically homogeneous, single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi and its high-entropy derivatives typically have coercive fields below 100 Oe.
A controlled thermal annealing step will transform chemically disordered fcc material into a partially L1₀-ordered state.
L1₀-like ordering can be induced within the fcc matrix without forming secondary phases.
The structural mediator is the formation of chemically ordered L1₀-type domains or nanostructures within the initially disordered lattice.
Atomic ordering reduces the cubic symmetry of the material.
The reduced symmetry associated with atomic ordering increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The enhanced anisotropy and ordered domains create additional domain-wall pinning centers.
The increased anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will raise the coercive field.
Annealing-induced ordering will largely retain the alloy's high saturation magnetization.
Annealing could increase coercivity several-fold, from below 100 Oe to a few hundred Oe.
An inert or reducing atmosphere will prevent oxidation during annealing.
Excessive annealing temperature or time could cause phase separation or grain growth.
Phase separation or excessive grain growth could reduce the beneficial magnetic properties.
X-ray diffraction superlattice reflections can be used as signatures of L1₀-type ordering.
Transmission electron microscopy can be used to observe the proposed ordered nanostructures.
Vibrating sample magnetometry can be used to compare coercivity and saturation magnetization between annealed and control samples.
The quantitative coercivity increase depends on annealing parameters, composition, grain size, and residual disorder.
